verdicts.reason: A drops the FREE / LIMITED SPOTS badges to the bottom-left below the CTA, where they are tiny, cut off from the headline they qualify and out of reading order. The oversized logo also outweighs the headline. B puts the badges above the headline, where they read better and are more legible, but its 17px left margin is cramped, its logo also dominates, and there is a dead band under the CTA.

The two are nearly identical. In both, the logo is huge and competes with the headline, and the tiny badges are stranded at the bottom below the CTA. A keeps a more comfortable 30px side margin. B's 17px margin pushes the headline and body copy close to the left edge, and its badges are slightly smaller.

A is the original banner shrunk into a thin strip across the middle of a tall canvas. The body copy and badge text are microscopic, the logo is unreadable, and about 85% of the canvas is empty: it was not rearranged at all. B is worse. The headline, body copy and badges are scattered into disconnected rows with large gaps, the text is still microscopic, and the reading order is broken.

A breaks the layout apart. The headline floats alone, the body copy sits squeezed between the logo and the CTA in tiny type, the badges are stranded far below, and most of the canvas is empty. B is a real vertical rearrangement: badges, headline, body copy, logo, then CTA, with an even 30px margin. Its flaws are a logo that outweighs the headline, small badge text, and a dead area under the CTA.
